Real Estate Default theme UPGRADING to 1.0.0
Liberu Real Estate scope
nodes.rationale: The scope covers agency operations end to end (properties, parties, listings, viewings, offers, progression, lettings, management, marketing, portal reporting) so that each capability is a separately releasable boundary rather than one monolithic estate-agency application.

nodes.label: Framework-neutral core boundary
nodes.rationale: Each capability has exactly one core boundary that carries no presentation framework, so the domain can be consumed by API, Filament or Livewire adapters interchangeably and the same rules hold whichever surface is installed.

nodes.label: One-to-one adapter rule
nodes.rationale: Adapters are optional and map one-to-one onto a core package, so a surface can be added or dropped without touching the domain and no adapter accumulates behaviour for more than one capability.

nodes.label: Real Estate delivery order (three phases)
nodes.rationale: Delivery is sequenced so that the core transaction chain lands first, then progression/marketing/reporting, then lettings and management — later phases depend on contracts the earlier ones establish.

nodes.label: Delivery phase 1: core transaction chain and website feed
Delivery phase 2: progression, portals, marketing, reporting, documents
Delivery phase 3: lettings, management, accounting, owner/tenant portals
Team-scoped, authorization-aware, auditable records
nodes.rationale: All records are team-scoped, authorization-aware, auditable and subject to retention and recovery rules — a single cross-cutting invariant asserted for every capability rather than re-decided per module.

nodes.label: Replaceable provider integration adapters
nodes.rationale: Provider integrations belong in replaceable adapters rather than core packages, so a third-party portal or transport can be swapped without a domain change and provider credentials never leak into the core.

nodes.label: 'planned' as an explicit backlog marker
nodes.rationale: Rows marked planned are explicit backlog items, not claims of implementation — the table is honest about what does not exist so a reader cannot mistake a roadmap entry for a shipped package.

nodes.label: Adapters stay planned until core contracts exist
nodes.rationale: Remaining API, Filament and Livewire adapters are deliberately marked planned until their matching core contracts exist, so no adapter is published against a boundary that has not been settled.

nodes.label: Foundation adapters vs product scope
nodes.rationale: Shared panel and interactive adapters are supplied by the foundation packages while product resources and components stay under their owning project scope, keeping product features out of the shared foundation.

nodes.label: Real Estate capability: Real Estate Core
Real Estate capability: Media and Documents
Real Estate capability: Portals and Reporting
Portal integrations are independently releasable
nodes.rationale: Each provider integration ships apart from real-estate-portals-reporting and does not depend on it, so a provider can be released, replaced or removed on its own schedule; the integration packages own the team-scoped synchronization state and payload contracts instead of pushing them into the reporting module.

nodes.label: Replaceable provider credentials and transport
nodes.rationale: Credentials and transport implementations stay behind a replaceable boundary so swapping a provider's HTTP client or account never reaches the domain.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/boilerplate-scripts
nodes.rationale: Release and maintenance automation is generic and shipped as a dev dependency rather than copied per meta repository, so every Composer-based meta repo whose modules and themes live in independent GitHub repositories runs the same tooling.

nodes.label: .liberu-meta.json meta-repository config
nodes.rationale: One copied-and-customized config carries organization, genre, repository, component paths, prefixes and extra Composer packages, so the scripts stay generic.

nodes.label: setup.sh
nodes.rationale: Performs a repeatable local or production install without destructive migrations.

nodes.label: update.sh
nodes.rationale: Updates dependencies and validates the project; --release 1.2.3 only commits, tags, pushes and creates the GitHub release after the checks succeed.

nodes.label: scripts/fleet
nodes.rationale: Fans a command across the component repositories once those repositories are the source of truth. tag is deliberately separate and only ever acts on an explicit --only list, because a tag is what gets published while a push is recoverable.

nodes.label: publish-components (removed)
nodes.rationale: Rsynced a monorepo into its component repositories — the opposite direction, and meaningless once those repositories are the source of truth. Replaced by fleet.

nodes.label: set-coverage-thresholds
nodes.rationale: Writes each measured figure into the package's tests.yml, ratcheting only upward — a package that has lost coverage keeps its threshold and is reported rather than silently lowered.

nodes.label: measure-coverage
nodes.rationale: Resolves each package from nothing and runs its own suite under pcov, so the figure is evidence from a standalone resolution rather than the host's.

nodes.label: measure-phpstan
nodes.rationale: Finds the highest level each package's src/ passes by bisection over a standalone resolution; levels are monotone, so four runs settle it instead of eleven.

nodes.label: set-phpstan-levels
nodes.rationale: Writes each measured level into tests.yml as the reusable workflow's phpstan-level input, ratcheting only upward and preserving the existing coverage-threshold.

nodes.label: Upward-only quality ratchet
nodes.rationale: Both coverage thresholds and PHPStan levels are per-package figures that only ever rise; a regression is reported instead of relaxing the gate.

nodes.label: Non-interactive, fail-on-error commands
nodes.rationale: All commands are non-interactive and fail on errors so they can run unattended in CI.

nodes.label: Packagist credentials from the environment
nodes.rationale: PACKAGIST_USERNAME and PACKAGIST_API_TOKEN are read from the environment and must never be committed; GitHub operations require an authenticated gh CLI.

nodes.label: Component repositories are the source of truth
nodes.rationale: Modules, themes and shared tooling live in independent GitHub repositories; the meta repository is Composer output, which is what makes a monorepo-to-package sync meaningless and a fan-out runner correct.

nodes.label: theme.json manifest
nodes.rationale: The manifest is the single declared surface for name, type, parent and asset entry points; it is the only asset entry-point index, so build inputs are derived from it rather than listed twice.

nodes.label: Theme parent inheritance chain
nodes.rationale: A public theme declares base as its parent and resolves missing views and assets up the chain, so only the shared root has to ship every layout.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/composer-installer
nodes.rationale: A trusted installer places each theme package under /themes/<name>; Composer and its lock file remain the source of version truth and the installed directory is committed by the host.

nodes.label: Presentation-only package boundary
nodes.rationale: A theme carries no domain behaviour — that stays in modules — and the host keeps control of theme selection and fallback, so a theme can never become a place where business rules hide.

nodes.label: Safe theme fallback
nodes.rationale: Hosts must retain a working base/default theme so that an unavailable optional asset or capability degrades instead of breaking the page.

nodes.label: Theme accessibility baseline
nodes.rationale: Keyboard access, visible focus, semantic landmarks, readable contrast, reduced motion, zoom/reflow and system-font fallbacks are required of every theme, not optional polish.

nodes.label: Host Vite build of theme entry points
nodes.rationale: vite.config.js derives its inputs from themes/*/theme.json, so installing a theme is enough to get it built — and a directory rename changes the input set, requiring a rebuild.

nodes.label: No bundled third-party assets without provenance
nodes.rationale: Themes ship their own sources only; any font, image, icon, video or template added later must carry its licence and attribution.

nodes.label: Theme testing expectations
nodes.rationale: Manifest parsing, provider registration, production asset compilation, supported host surfaces, responsive layout, keyboard navigation, contrast and fallback are all validated, and visual changes carry before/after evidence.

nodes.label: Unpublished theme preview image
nodes.rationale: No maintained preview is published yet; one must be added under .github/assets/ before claiming visual-regression coverage.

nodes.label: Private security disclosure (security@liberusoftware.com)
nodes.rationale: Vulnerabilities must not be reported through public issues.

nodes.label: base theme (Liberu Base)
nodes.rationale: Shared semantic tokens, accessible layout and progressive presentation primitives live at the shared root so every public theme inherits one accessible baseline.

nodes.label: default theme (Liberu Default)
nodes.rationale: Neutral public and portal defaults built on Liberu Base.

nodes.label: dark theme (Liberu Dark)
nodes.rationale: Dark, reduced-glare presentation with a system fallback.

nodes.label: clear-signal theme (Clear Signal)
nodes.rationale: Teal signal on a quiet neutral workbench.

nodes.label: real-estate-default theme
nodes.rationale: Presentation only: it composes the default and base parents, owns real-estate visual identity and view composition, and never queries module tables, replaces policies or implements domain workflows.

nodes.label: Declared supported host surfaces
nodes.rationale: A theme names the host surfaces it supports (application.shell, identity.auth, foundation.account, blog.index) so a host can tell before installing which screens it actually covers.

nodes.label: Theme rename: liberu-base becomes base (2.0)
nodes.rationale: standards/THEMES.md derives both the repository name and the install path from one {name}, and this theme carried three different ones. A theme's name is a stable manifest surface, so making the manifest agree with the unchanged Composer package name is a major release.

nodes.label: standards/THEMES.md
nodes.rationale: Derives repository name and install path from a single {name}, which is why three divergent names counted as a defect.

nodes.label: ThemeDiscovery realpath dedupe
nodes.rationale: Discovery merges the tracked tree with Composer's installed theme packages and dedupes by realpath — so mid-wave a stale themes/liberu-base and a fresh themes/base do not dedupe and two themes appear until the stale directory is removed.

nodes.label: Child-theme relative CSS import across install dirs
nodes.rationale: A child theme importing the shared root by path crosses the install directory, so a rename of the parent directory moves the import path with it.

nodes.label: Real-estate theme extension points
nodes.rationale: Stable named slots (real-estate.properties.card/grid/search, modules.real-estate.properties.show, module-extension-points) let a theme compose views while module actions, validation, authorization, API contracts and Livewire state stay owned by their packages.

nodes.label: Semantic design tokens (Tailwind v4 + CSS custom properties)
nodes.rationale: Components consume semantic tokens rather than hard-coded brand values, so canvas, surface, text, focus, state, typography, spacing, motion and layering can be re-themed without touching components.

nodes.label: Asset budgets: 80 KiB CSS / 40 KiB JS compressed
nodes.rationale: The manifest is the only asset entry-point index and generated output is not committed; the budget keeps the built theme small enough for a portal front end.

nodes.label: LTR/RTL logical properties and translated strings
Graceful operation without JavaScript and reduced motion
Empty server-rendered state when a module is absent
nodes.rationale: Missing optional modules and unavailable real-estate data render empty states rather than errors, so the theme works on a compatible non-optimized host.

nodes.label: No analytics, embeds or external media
nodes.rationale: The theme carries no credentials, analytics, advertising, external embeds or privileged data; CSP, CSRF, consent and secure asset delivery remain host responsibilities, and Blade escapes output by default.

nodes.label: Semantic versioning over tokens, slots, view names, entry points
nodes.rationale: Breaking changes to tokens, slots, view names or asset entry points require a major version, because those are the surfaces a consuming host builds against.

nodes.label: Pest 5 suite and Install/Tests/Visual/Compatibility workflows
nodes.rationale: The independent repository runs its own workflows; visual evidence covers responsive CSS, reduced motion, forced colors, RTL and semantic markup, with browser screenshots deferred until the host's visual runner exists.

nodes.label: Do not edit installed files under themes/
nodes.rationale: Installed theme directories are Composer output; a local edit is overwritten by the next update, so selection goes through the manifest and THEME_* host configuration.

hyperedges.label: One core boundary plus its one-to-one API, Filament and Livewire adapters
real-estate-default inherits default, then base, then host fallback
